answer: A public company registry can do quiet sybil work. Each operator links its seats to a Legal Entity Identifier checked against the open GLEIF database, and one LEI backs at most 5 seats (assumed). An LEI costs about $80 a year and lists directors a court can reach (assumed figures), so a 1,000-seat farm needs 200 renewed entities, each a paper trail. A fish co-op on a wharf qualifies as easily as a firm atop a glass summit. It is not proof as solid as basalt, but faking it in bulk is slow and traceable.
